summary.intent: Serve as an autonomous release engineer for CipherBox v2: triage the issue backlog into parallel, file-disjoint PR batches, launch worktree agents to implement them, and manage the CodeRabbit/Greptile/macroscope review queue (including overnight) while never merging or flipping PRs ready without explicit user approval.
summary.outcome: Landed multiple waves of PRs (6+ merged overnight, wave 4 of 6 draft PRs launched and now in review), closed ~45+ issues, restored and hardened branch protection, resolved the #1025/#1026 design blockers via two merged ADRs in cipher-box-next, shipped a tracker-ref cleanup PR with a permanent CI guard, and committed custom macroscope review-agent configs in draft PR #1089.

repo: cargo check/test --workspace never builds or runs the wasm32 targets; wasm32 usize is 4 bytes (not 8), causing copy_from_slice/to_be_bytes panics invisible to native tests — must explicitly run cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-wasip1.

CodeRabbit posts clean verdicts ('No actionable comments...') by editing a single mutable status comment in place; findings land in a separate submitted review body. A poller must check both surfaces and fence on a timestamp taken at flip-time, or it will read stale/fresh verdicts wrong.
CodeRabbit bot login is 'coderabbitai[bot]', not 'coderabbitai' — filtering on the wrong string makes the status-comment surface invisible.

CodeRabbit is incremental and dedupes by head SHA: a walkthrough (even fair-usage-gated) marks a SHA 'Already reviewed' forever; `@coderabbitai full review` is the only override and itself needs quota.

macroscope reviews are ready-gated (post-user config change) but were initially draft-inclusive; its findings are posted as inline PR comments with an empty review body, so a review-body-only poller misses them entirely.
tools/hw-gates and tools/mock-ipns-routing are standalone Cargo workspaces — `cargo fmt --all` from the repo root never touches them, so formatting debris there is invisible to root-level CI.

GitHub Actions staging deploy vars (VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER, STAGING_API_URL) live at the 'staging' environment scope, not repo scope; jobs without `environment:` (e.g. web-e2e.yml) only ever see repo-scope vars.

main had zero branch protection prior to this session — the merge button reported check status without gating on it. Required Result-aggregator contexts (not individual matrix legs) must be used for path-filtered jobs to avoid deadlock.
The v2 rotation/grant crypto design decisions (ADRs) live in FSM1/cipher-box-next `decisions/`, not in this repo's dead `docs/adr/` (v1 residue, describes a retired AES-256-GCM primitive).

Issue numbers in FSM1/cipher-box share one ever-increasing counter with PRs and passed 1000 long ago, so any bare `#NN` with 1-2 digits can only refer to the FSM1/cipher-box-next wayfinder decision corpus (issues 23-39), never a local ticket — this makes the tracker-ref guard's 3-digit floor permanent and principled.

AGENTS.md rule 8 (encode/decode fail-closed symmetry) and the 'never apply a review suggestion literally' rule repeatedly caught real vulnerabilities: literal application of reviewer suggestions twice introduced denial-of-revocation / availability regressions that only surfaced because agents re-ran their own review gates on their fixes.

A comment naming a tracking issue is a claim about the tracker's state, which drifts independently of the code; 91% of ~450 such refs in the repo pointed at closed issues. Fixed with scripts/check-tracker-refs.mjs, a merge-blocking 'Tracker Refs' CI check.

code.finding: sweep_pass's epoch-lag predicate operates on scope roots, but a scope root can never lag its own floor (rotate.rs/cascade.rs always publish-then-raise-floor) — the sweep was walking the wrong population, making create_read_grant's SubtreeNotConverged gate unconditionally pass (unenforced) until ADR 0003's interior-node retarget.

ChildRef.ipns_name lives in the read body, so a write-plane name wave (rotateScopeWrite) cannot leave the read body byte-stable — parent refs must be rewritten (ADR 0004), contradicting the module's stated 'read plane untouched' claim.

Carried history links were copied verbatim across a re-seal, keeping the prior rotator's signature at the old epoch while the gate recomputes at the current epoch — rotating a scope twice made it permanently unadoptable; fixed by re-minting the detached signature at the current read epoch.

RacingTransport test decorator implemented RecordTransport against the pre-fork 3-parameter get_record; adding a required max_bytes param elsewhere caused a semantic merge conflict invisible to git (both sides mergeable, combination failed to compile).
CachedSeed doc comment went stale after commit 8df73df73 changed seed provenance stamping logic — a classic case of a comment surviving a behavioral rewrite.
Module header excluded 'content bytes' from scope, but the module had since grown a full content plane (publish_update_content, upload_version/blocks) — comment contradicted the code it annotated.

Regex bound #\d{3,5} is load-bearing on both ends: upper bound rejects 6/8-digit hex colors, lower bound (3 digits) is what makes bare #NN wayfinder decision citations exempt without an explicit allowlist.

workflow: For overnight/unattended CodeRabbit slot management: schedule flips using absolute epoch seconds, never HHMM string comparisons (a numeric HHMM compare can be trivially true across midnight and fire jobs early, burning slots).

Space review-slot retries from the previous verdict's landing time plus a safety margin (user specified 70 min, not 60), never from 'now' — spacing from now can land inside the still-active rate-limit window.

Always verify a delegated sub-agent's self-reported claims against the actual code/diff before relaying them to the user (caught false 'wasm fix complete', false 'no collision', a bad --no-verify justification, and two cases where an agent overstepped its file-ownership brief).
Before launching parallel worktree agents on a shared repo, fast-forward local main first — agents fork local HEAD, so a stale local main silently drops recent merges from their base.
When splitting a PR post-review (e.g. #1021 crypto vs mechanical), resume the original authoring agent rather than doing fresh git surgery — it retains commit-level context.
Batch parallel PRs by file/module ownership, not by issue count — a single hot file (facade.rs, write_plane.rs, net/rotation.rs) caps real parallelism regardless of how many issues are 'free'.

Verify merge order not by reasoning about line-number shifts, but by actually building the combined merge tree (git merge-tree + cargo check/test) — line-number-based conflict predictions were wrong twice.
Use tracked background Bash/Agent tasks instead of nohup for anything needing a completion notification — nohup survives but is invisible to the harness.

friction: Repeated intermittent GitHub API/network connectivity failures ('connection refused') throughout the night, requiring retry loops with connectivity checks before every push/API call.

Self-inflicted scheduling bug (numeric HHMM comparison) caused two PRs to flip ready inside the CodeRabbit rate-limit window, costing a review slot and, for one PR, its entire automatic review trigger (SHA-dedup) until an explicit full-review override was used.

CodeRabbit poller had two consecutive bugs (bot-login string mismatch, stale-verdict reuse without a timestamp fence) that caused a clean review to be misdiagnosed as 'never reviewed', triggering wasted retry requests that overwrote the only record of the clean verdict.
Local stale node_modules caused false-red typecheck/test failures on a full main verification, requiring diagnosis before trusting the 'red' result.

Macroscope's Ticket Requirements agent config uses a Jira/Linear-style ticket regex (`[A-Za-z]+-\d+`) that doesn't match this repo's GitHub-issue (`#1234`) or branch-naming conventions, so it will silently no-op on every current PR.
Manual review passes (/simplify, /security-review, /crypto-privacy-review) had to be run as ad-hoc sub-agents because those skills weren't installed in the environment for one PR.
open_items: Wave 5 (the #635 rotation critical path): #1026 must land first (RepublishedNode shape change), then #1025, then the four trigger.rs issues — deliberately held out of wave 4 due to rotation/ hot-file contention with PR-6.
#1090 — pre-request BYO policy verdicts (InvalidEndpoint, InsecureTransport, etc.) incorrectly charge the attempt budget instead of holding, dead-lettering content after a typo'd endpoint.
#1083 — leadership token published in cleartext on origin-wide BroadcastChannel; cb:bye has no sender authentication, enabling same-origin MITM/reclaim.
#1087 — FilesPage route guard hangs indefinitely on a stalled session provider instead of redirecting; this bug forced two e2e assertions in #1078 to be weakened.
#1088 — Web Bundle and Web E2E Smoke CI jobs each rebuild the same WASM; cargo cache omits the host build tree causing proc-macro recompilation every run.
#1073 — WASM host boundary flattens all six OverBudgetCause variants into one 'overBudget' code, blocking full cause-distinct UI rendering (used by #1075).
#1075 — nothing in apps/web reads SnapshotDescriptor.blocked, so drain-held ops show no explanation.

#1076 / #1077 — ascent-link seed threading not independently authenticated; scope root can grow past what its own re-seal can author (HeadTooLarge stall on the size axis, deliberately not made fatal to avoid a denial-of-revocation vector).
#1069 — web half of #1006 (recoverable-error UI classification) never implemented despite the client-side plumbing existing.
docs/adr/ in cipher-box is dead v1 residue describing a retired AES-256-GCM primitive — flagged for a cleanup issue but not filed.
Web E2E Smoke Result CI context exists and passes but is not yet added to main's required status checks.
PR #1089 (macroscope custom review agents) is still draft/unmerged; being edited (architecture-standards.md) as the transcript ends.
Full four/five/six-way combined-tree verification needs re-running once wave 4's PRs' review-fix commits land, per the established pattern from prior waves.

~300 remaining stale tracker refs outside crates/apps/packages/landing/tools/scripts/.github (if any) and the broader repo-wide qualification of two-digit wayfinder refs were both explicitly decided as NOT needed (confirmed correct, closed threads).
